-95.44850,29.75180.name: Kindbody - Houston
-95.44850,29.75180.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Toral  Parikh, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-93.83629,32.33321.name: Chimp Haven, Inc.
-93.83629,32.33321.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-123.22899,49.24835.name: TRIUMF Inc.
-123.22899,49.24835.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, April 2026
-123.22899,49.24835.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, April 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

5.66500,51.96700.name: KeyGene
5.66500,51.96700.desc: A Dutch crop research company that develops breeding and editing technologies and licenses them to seed companies rather than selling seed itself. It is the layer beneath the visible market — the traits and techniques in other companies’ varieties often originate here, so the concentration measured by counting seed brands understates how few sources the underlying technology has.

-51.16000,-23.31000.name: TMG — Tropical Melhoramento & Genética
-51.16000,-23.31000.desc: A Brazilian soy breeding foundation funded by the farmers who use its varieties, licensing traits from the majors and putting them into cultivars bred for Brazilian soils and daylength. It is the arrangement that made Brazilian soy competitive: the trait comes from abroad and the adaptation is done at home, which is also why trait licensing revenue leaves the country while the breeding value stays.

-0.09000,51.51400.name: Legal & General / institutional stewardship
-0.09000,51.51400.desc: A large asset manager that publishes its voting record and engages companies on governance, including in agriculture and pharmaceuticals. Stewardship of this kind is the only routine mechanism by which an owner questions a company's conduct between scandals, and it operates through private meetings with a public voting record attached.

-94.20900,36.36300.name: Walmart
-94.20900,36.36300.desc: The largest grocery retailer in the world. Its sourcing standards travel upstream through suppliers who cannot afford to lose the account, which makes a retail purchasing policy one of the few instruments that changes agricultural practice across borders without any legal force at all.

106.82000,10.95000.name: Nafovanny
106.82000,10.95000.desc: Described as the largest captive primate breeding facility in the world, supplying long-tailed macaques to testing laboratories, and established in 1994 by a Hong Kong company. It sits in the country that absorbed part of the demand when Chinese and then Cambodian supply closed. A single facility of that scale is worth marking because of what the rest of this facet has established: the paperwork accompanying a laboratory macaque describes a category rather than a chain, and analysts examining reported breeding rates across the region have argued that the figures returned by several farms exceed what is biologically plausible for the volumes shipped. Whether or not that analysis holds for any particular farm, it can only be tested against facility-level records, which is why the facilities need naming.
